audit_findings.title: Unbounded asbestos funding claim is outside the valuation bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $545.0 million proposed trust funding, including the $270.0 million QSF already funded; remaining expected obligation and adverse-case exposure unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any funding not already expensed through continuing owner earnings or supplied by Aldrich, Murray, the QSF, or insurance is a common-equity bridge deduction; continuing legal costs also reduce prospective OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We cannot ensure that Aldrich and Murray can successfully reorganize, nor can we give any assurances as to the amount of the ultimate obligations under Funding Agreements pursuant to which certain subsidiaries are obligated, among other things, to pay the costs and expenses of Aldrich and Murray during the pendency of the Chapter 11 cases to the extent distributions from their respective subsidiaries are insufficient to do so and to provide an amount for the funding for a trust established pursuant to section 524(g) of the Bankruptcy Code, to the extent that the other assets of Aldrich and Murray are insufficient to provide the requisite trust funding or any plan of reorganization, or the resulting impact on our financial condition, results of operations or future prospects.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: the bridge deducts no asbestos obligation even though subsidiaries remain contractually responsible for trust shortfalls and case costs. The filed plan implies $275.0 million above the existing QSF before other assets and insurance, while challenges to the restructuring leave the adverse case unbounded. That unresolved exposure is reasonably capable of materially reducing equity value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the QSF, Aldrich and Murray assets, insurance recoveries, accrued Funding Agreement amounts, proposed trust funding and continuing legal costs; deduct the probability-weighted amount not already captured in OE and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not be fully distributable without tax leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: The entire $1,318.3 million cash bridge equals $5.90 per share and 3.0% of $44,589 million base equity value; the filing separately estimates $401.9 million of tax if relevant permanently reinvested earnings are distributed
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, restrictions or operating cash requirements reduce the $1,318.3 million cash addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, no deferred taxes have been provided for earnings of certain of the Company's subsidiaries, since these earnings have been and under current plans will continue to be permanently reinvested in these subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The distributable portion and associated tax are unresolved, so no specific error is demonstrated. Nevertheless, even removing the entire cash bridge—not merely the possible tax leakage—would reduce base value from $199.66 to about $193.76 per share and would not change the conclusion relative to the $445.19 market price.
audit_findings.action: Identify the jurisdiction, permanent-reinvestment status and minimum operating requirement of the June 2026 cash, then replace the bridge addition with after-tax distributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded employee-benefit claims may not be fully reflected in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $194.6 million pension deficit plus $217.0 million OPEB obligation, totaling $411.6 million or $1.84 per share and 0.9% of base equity value; projected 2026 pension contributions are $84 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Any benefit deficit or recurring cash contribution exceeding the benefit cost already included in OE reduces prospective OE or requires a separate equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company currently projects that it will contribute approximately $84 million to its plans worldwide in 2026, a portion of which may be funded by assets held in an employer-owned trust.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate that the valuation omitted an economic claim because benefit expense is present in earnings and the balance-sheet obligations are recognized. Even a conservative separate deduction of the full $411.6 million disclosed pension and OPEB amount would reduce base value by only $1.84 per share and would not alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Map pension and OPEB expense, cash contributions, trust-funded amounts and benefit payments into each OE year; deduct only the economic deficit or prospective cash shortfall not already captured, avoiding double counting.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-accounting gains may inflate the OE trend
audit_findings.magnitude: $61.2 million in 2025, $25.0 million in 2024 and $49.3 million in 2023, totaling $135.5 million pre-tax; the total is 5.2% of the $2,610.2 million anchor and each annual item is no more than 2.2% of that year's supplied OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, nonrecurring contingent-consideration gains overstate historical OE observations and therefore the log-trend anchor and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, non-cash adjustments to contingent consideration reduced Selling and administrative expenses for the years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 by $61.2 million and $25.0 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the gains were removed is unresolved, so an OE construction error is not yet demonstrated. Their filed gross amount is small relative to the anchor, is spread across only three of nine trend observations and, even under the conservative comparison of the entire $135.5 million with the anchor, cannot close the gap between the $199.66 base value and the $445.19 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reverse each contingent-consideration gain using its actual tax treatment in the 2023-2025 OE observations, recompute the log-trend anchor and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation shares are missing from the denominator ceiling
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsettled ordinary-share equivalents increase fully diluted shares and reduce every scenario's value per share and buy-below price without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Any amounts invested in ordinary share equivalents will be settled in ordinary shares of the Company at the time of distribution.
audit_findings.explanation: Settlement in ordinary shares is demonstrated, but the filing excerpt supplies neither the outstanding share-equivalent balance nor evidence that it is already included in the 223.322068 million denominator. The direction is adverse, but the record cannot establish whether the dilution is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the period-end deferred-compensation account balance and conversion terms, calculate unsettled ordinary-share equivalents, remove duplicates already included in incentive-plan dilution, and rerun per-share values and buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: A one-time pension settlement charge may depress historical OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.2 million pre-tax in continuing operations, equal to 0.7% of the $2,610.2 million anchor and 0.6% of 2025 OE; approximately $13.9 million after tax using the filed 19.2% 2025 effective rate
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the non-cash settlement charge understates 2025 OE and slightly lowers the log-trend anchor and operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the transaction, the Company recognized a pre-tax non-cash settlement charge of $35.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, of which $17.2 million was recorded in Continuing Operations and $17.9 million was recorded in Discontinued Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates the nonrecurring charge but not whether the OE calculation retained it. Even full reversal is less than 1% of the anchor before the further dilution caused by using a nine-observation trend, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the 2025 OE reconciliation, reverse only the $17.2 million continuing-operations settlement charge using its actual tax treatment if it remains included, recompute the trend anchor and rerun all scenarios.
